name: Sony WH-1000XM5 Wireless Noise Cancelling Headphones
verdict: The best over-ear headphones overall — reference sound, class-leading noise cancellation, and all-day comfort.
description: The Sony WH-1000XM5 remain the benchmark premium wireless headphones. Two processors drive eight microphones for noise cancellation that silences planes, trains, and offices, and the 30mm carbon-fiber drivers deliver detailed, balanced sound that works across every genre. Up to 30 hours of battery with ANC gets through long-haul travel, and LDAC streams high-res audio from Android. The lightweight headband and soft earcups are among the most comfortable for marathon listening. Between sound, ANC, and comfort, nothing else balances all three this well.
pros: Among the best noise cancellation available

name: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones
verdict: The best noise cancellation money can buy — Bose's ANC is still the gold standard, now with Immersive Audio.
description: Bose wrote the book on noise cancellation, and the QuietComfort Ultra Headphones are its best work. ANC performance is the best available — low-frequency airplane rumble, mid-range office chatter, and high-frequency fan whine all fade away more effectively than with any competitor. Immersive Audio adds spatial depth to music, and CustomTune calibrates the sound to your ear shape on every wear. Up to 24 hours of battery, legendary comfort, and the best ANC make these the headphones for frequent travelers.
pros: Immersive Audio adds real spatial depth
cons: Among the priciest on this list
Sound trails Sony for some purists

name: Sennheiser Momentum 4 Wireless Headphones
verdict: The best-sounding wireless headphones — Sennheiser's tuning delivers the most natural, detailed sound in this roundup.
description: If sound quality is your top priority, the Sennheiser Momentum 4 wins. Sennheiser has made audiophile equipment for decades, and it shows. The 42mm drivers deliver the most natural, detailed sound of any wireless headphone here — instruments have texture, vocals have presence, and the soundstage is wide. ANC is good (not quite Bose-level, but effective), and 60 hours of battery is extraordinary — charge once every couple of weeks. Premium materials and a comfortable fit make them travel-ready, and at $300 they're a value for audio enthusiasts.
features: Sennheiser Smart Control app with EQ
pros: Best sound quality in wireless headphones

name: Apple AirPods Max (USB-C)
verdict: The best headphones for Apple users — USB-C, premium build, and the deepest integration with iPhone, iPad, and Mac.
description: The AirPods Max with USB-C update the original with a modern port and new colors while keeping what made them special: a stunning anodized-aluminum-and-steel build, effective active noise cancellation, and Personalized Spatial Audio with head tracking for immersive movies and music. For anyone deep in the Apple ecosystem, the seamless switching between iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple TV is unmatched, and audio sharing and hands-free Siri just work. They're heavy and pricey, but no headphone integrates better with Apple devices.
features: USB-C charging and new color options
Personalized Spatial Audio with head tracking
Anodized aluminum and stainless steel build
pros: Immersive spatial audio with head tracking
cons: Among the most expensive on this list

name: Anker Soundcore Q20i Wireless Headphones
verdict: The cheapest ANC headphones worth buying — hybrid noise cancellation, 40-hour battery, and Hi-Res Audio for around $35.
description: The Soundcore Q20i make you question why anyone spends $400. For around $35 you get hybrid active noise cancellation (not just passive), up to 40 hours of battery with ANC on, Hi-Res Audio certification over wire, and a comfortable over-ear design. The bass is emphasized — great for pop and hip-hop — and while the ANC won't match Sony or Bose, it genuinely reduces commute and office noise. It's a long-running Amazon best-seller. For the price of a nice lunch, you get legitimate wireless ANC headphones.
features: Up to 40-hour battery with ANC on
pros: App EQ at this price is rare
cons: ANC is basic vs premium brands

name: Sony WH-CH720N Wireless Noise Cancelling Headphones
verdict: The best mid-range ANC headphones — Sony's noise cancellation and sound quality for around $100.
description: The WH-CH720N brings Sony's noise cancellation down to an accessible price. The Integrated Processor V1 handles ANC, and the sound carries Sony's warm, detailed tuning. At just 192g they're the lightest headphones here — you barely feel them during long sessions. Up to 35 hours of battery with ANC, multipoint Bluetooth for two devices, and quick charging round out a compelling mid-range package. Around $100 on sale, they're the sweet spot between budget and premium.
features: Sony Integrated Processor V1 for ANC

name: JBL Tune 770NC Wireless Headphones
verdict: The best headphones under $100 — adaptive ANC, 70-hour battery, and JBL's fun sound signature.
description: JBL's Tune 770NC pack a staggering 70 hours of battery into a sub-$100 package. Adaptive noise cancellation adjusts to your environment, and Smart Ambient lets you control how much outside sound you hear. The JBL sound signature is bass-forward and energetic — great for workout playlists and pop. The foldable, lightweight design makes them travel-friendly, and the JBL app offers a full EQ and ANC customization. At $80, they compete with headphones twice their price on battery alone.
features: JBL Headphones app with full EQ
pros: 70-hour battery is unmatched at the price
Adaptive ANC works well for the money

name: Beats Studio Pro Wireless Headphones
verdict: The best headphones for both iPhone and Android — USB-C lossless audio and full features on both platforms.
description: Beats Studio Pro solve a common problem: most premium headphones favor either Apple or Android. The Studio Pro work well with both. iPhone users get spatial audio and seamless pairing; Android users get the Beats app and solid codec support. USB-C lossless audio (wired) delivers clean sound regardless of platform. ANC is effective, the sound is balanced with Beats' signature punch, and up to 40 hours of battery handles a work week. At $250 (frequently on sale for less), they're among the best cross-platform premium headphones.
features: Full features on both iPhone AND Android

name: Anker Soundcore Life Q30 Wireless Headphones
verdict: The best budget ANC headphones for sound customization — hybrid ANC, parametric EQ, and 50-hour battery for under $60.
description: The Soundcore Life Q30 have been a budget ANC staple for years. Hybrid ANC with multiple modes adapts to your environment, and the Soundcore app offers a parametric EQ so you can tune the sound exactly — a feature missing from most budget headphones. Up to 50 hours of battery in ANC mode (60 without) means charging twice a month at most. Hi-Res certification over wire and a foldable travel case round it out. Under $60, they're the headphones to beat.
cons: Bass can be boomy without EQ

name: SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset
verdict: The best headset for gaming — dual wireless, hot-swappable batteries, and ANC that works for both gaming and music.
description: The Arctis Nova Pro Wireless is the headset gamers and remote workers dream about. Dual wireless connects to your PC or console over low-latency 2.4GHz AND your phone over Bluetooth simultaneously — game audio and phone calls at once. The two-battery system means zero downtime: swap a dead battery for a charged one in seconds. ANC is effective for both gaming immersion and office noise, and the retractable ClearCast Gen 2 mic is excellent. Premium drivers deliver detailed spatial audio for competitive play.
pros: ANC works for gaming AND office
cons: Base station needed for full features
